what_happened.line: The Finance Committee took no budget votes; it heard FY24 budget presentations from the town IT director and the police chief.
The police presentation covered a personnel line up about ten percent, lower overtime because of a hiring pause, and a reduced lockup line.
The IT director described higher costs for computers, Office 365 email, Munis and OpenGov software, and fiber for three buildings, and will research leasing versus buying.
The town manager reported bids, revised budget figures and a large increase in the Monty Tech assessment.
The chair will ask that a backup public hearing be posted for April 13th beside March 30th, and will send questions to state representatives ahead of a joint meeting.

why_it_matters: Police pay and IT software and fiber costs are recurring lines in the FY24 town budget, so increases there carry into later years' tax bills.
The Monty Tech assessment is set by the regional school, not by town vote, and its increase adds to what the town must raise.
Residents can speak at the public hearing on the budget, and the committee's questions to state representatives bear on state aid.
watch_next: Public hearing on the budget on March 30th, with a backup date of April 13th if the chair's request is posted.
The joint meeting with state representatives, for which the chair will send questions ahead of time.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. reconciliation.summary: Neither record shows a formal vote, and the main money figures agree: the $986,000 ARPA switch, the $1.5 million overlay reserve, the health insurance, Monty Tech, cherry sheet, bid and snow-and-ice figures. The official minutes are a partial summary. They leave out the whole police discussion and the follow-up items our minutes list, and they differ on the software maintenance figure and possibly the fiber internet figure.
